question.text: Surya Capital is structuring its new Cat II AIF and is considering appointing its group company 'Surya Custody Services Ltd.' (a SEBI-registered custodian) as the fund's custodian. As per SEBI (AIF) (Amendment) Regulations 2024, this is:

answer.text: Permitted automatically because both entities have the same SEBI registrations.
Permitted ONLY if specific conditions laid down by SEBI are fulfilled; otherwise the custodian shall not be a related party to the sponsor/manager/designated partners.
Permitted only for Cat III AIFs.

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI (AIF) (Amendment) Regulations 2024 w.e.f. 5-Jan-2024 provide: 'The custodian shall not be a related party to the sponsors or designated partners, UNLESS specific conditions are fulfilled.' This is a conditional permission — full compliance with the specified conditions (arm's-length governance, additional disclosures) is mandatory. The Trap: Option A is over-absolute. Option B ignores the related-party filter. Option D invents a category-specific carve-out. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C (Compliance) tests related-party transaction definitions under Companies Act and SEBI LODR. XIX-C frames it specifically for the custodian appointment. Manager's Pro-Tip: Even when group-custody is permitted, walk the LP through the governance safeguards in an LPAC side-letter. Large institutional LPs sometimes veto group-custodian arrangements even if SEBI permits.
